claim: CasaOS repo analysed at e099dd6b (pushed 2026-11-09); Apache-2.0; 37,621 stars; created 2021-09-26; last stable release v0.4.15 (2024-12-19)
ZimaOS GitHub repo has no LICENSE file and says it is 'just for releasing test images'; created 2023-09-26; 3,105 stars
ZimaOS 1.8.0 published 2026-10-15 with three x86_64-only assets: a 1.6 GB .raucb update bundle (901,614 downloads at access), an installer .img and an installer .iso
ZimaOS states it is built with Buildroot; the 1.8.0 rootfs glibc identifies itself as 'GNU C Library (Buildroot)'

IceWhale keeps a Buildroot fork whose 2026.02.x-zima branch is 6 commits ahead of upstream 2026.02.x: Docker engine/cli pinned back from 28.3.2 to 27.5.1, systemd custom-init handling, rust-bin, ca-certificates and runc 1.3.5 bumps
ZimaOS supported hardware: ZimaBoard, ZimaBoard 2, ZimaBlade, ZimaCube and generic x86-64 UEFI; installation requires Secure Boot to be disabled

ZimaOS installs from a USB installer image that erases the selected disk; the 1.8.0 installer image holds only a 72 MiB ESP and a 1,626 MiB 'installer-data' partition, so the target layout is written by the installer
The 1.8.0 update is a RAUC bundle in verity format with three slot images (boot.vfat 128 MiB, kernel.img, rootfs.img ~1.5 GB), compatible=zimaos-zimacube, and an install-check hook

Bundles are signed with a leaf certificate 'IceWhale Technology Development-1' (RSA-2048) issued by 'IceWhale Technology OTA Development'; both certificates are valid from 1970-01-01 to 9999-12-31 and both sit in the device keyring
ZimaOS RAUC system.conf: GRUB backend; A/B slot pairs kernel.0/rootfs.0 (bootname A) and kernel.1/rootfs.1 (bootname B); a single shared boot.0 vfat slot (casaos-boot) with allow-mounted=true
The boot slot is updated by a custom hook that copies the new files over the single live ESP with cp -rf, preserving only grubenv, so the bootloader itself is not A/B
ZimaOS GRUB picks the first slot in ORDER with OK=1 and TRY<3, increments TRY each boot, and falls back to a rescue-shell entry when no slot qualifies (BOOT_ATTEMPT_LIMIT=3)

Mark-good is zimaos-last.service, which runs 'rauc status mark-good' once zimaos.target (9 ZimaOS daemons) and mnt-boot are up and a disk-migration check passes; Docker apps, networking and data health are not part of the gate

The rootfs post-install hook runs data migrations (legacy apps, compose restart policy, app-repo metadata) on the running system before reboot, best-effort, so a later fallback to the old slot meets already-migrated data

The ZimaOS OTA feed rauc.txt lists GitHub and an Aliyun OSS mirror plus a checksums path; a workflow uploads rauc.txt to OSS on every push to main using tvrcgo/upload-to-oss@master (a branch, not a pinned SHA)
ZimaDocs: ZimaOS uses a dual-partition design (Slot A and Slot B, about 6 GB each); users switch slots manually in the GRUB menu; user data lives on a separate partition
ZimaOS offline update: place a .raucb from GitHub in /ZimaOS-HD/rauc/offline/

ZimaOS 1.8.0 rootfs is mounted read-only (fstab ro); a casaos-overlay ext4 partition carries /etc changes; /DATA and /var/lib/docker are bind mounts from /var/lib/casaos_data; systemd-sysext units are present; no k3s, kubectl or helm
ZimaOS 1.8.0 ships Linux kernel 6.18.9
CasaOS installs by a piped script on Debian 12, Ubuntu Server 20.04 or Raspberry Pi OS (official) on amd64, arm64 and armv7
The CasaOS installer downloads component tarballs with curl and extracts them without any checksum or signature check

On 2026-11-11 get.casaos.io served an 807-line 'v0.4.16' installer that matches no file in the public get repo and pins alpha components (Gateway v0.4.9-alpha4, AppManagement v0.4.10-alpha2); get.casaos.io/update returned HTTP 500
CasaOS self-update from the UI (POST /sys/update) runs 'curl -fsSL <UpdateUrl or https://get.casaos.io/update?t=MANUFACTURER> | bash' in a goroutine

CasaOS/ZimaOS app format is a Docker Compose file with an x-casaos extension at app level (id, architectures, main, category, port_map, index, version, descriptions) and service level (envs, ports, volumes descriptions)
The CasaOS app validator only checks that the x-casaos block exists and decodes into ComposeAppStoreInfo; no permission, privilege or network checks
If an app omits architectures, AppManagement assumes it supports all CPU architectures
App update copies the store's image tags into the local compose file and runs PullAndApply asynchronously; a failure only publishes an error event
PullAndApply backs up the compose file but sets success=true even when the new containers fail to start, so the compose file is restored only if pull or load fails; app data is never snapshotted
The app catalog refreshes when the HEAD Content-Length of the store zip changes, then downloads and unpacks it with no signature check
The official CasaOS-AppStore (Apache-2.0) has 182 app directories; its Home Assistant app uses network_mode: host and privileged: true
CasaOS identity: the user service signs ES256 (ECDSA) JWTs and publishes a JWKS endpoint for the gateway and other services; the user model carries a role string

ZimaOS pricing: Free has 4 disks and 3 members; ZimaOS+ is a USD 29 lifetime, device-bound license with unlimited disks and users, transferable after one year; official Zima devices auto-activate Plus
IceWhale states ZimaOS has 'zero telemetry and zero user data collection'
The CasaOS installer queries ifconfig.io/country_code to choose a China download mirror
ZimaOS product page: 'Supports all X86-64 hardware'; requirements x86-64 CPU, 4 GB RAM (8 GB recommended), 16 GB for the OS
Zima shop prices: ZimaBoard 2 832 USD 339 and 1664 USD 399 (board only); ZimaCube 2 USD 799 (i3-1215U/8 GB), USD 1,299 (i5-1235U/16 GB), USD 2,499 (64 GB + RTX Pro 2000)
ZimaOS AI features: 1.8.0 adds Gallery natural-language photo search; a zimaos-photos AI worker runs one NCNN inference at a time in a low-priority, OOM-first slice
ZimaOS-MCP is an external npx MCP server that logs in with the ZimaOS username and password from environment variables and exposes file tools only; no license file; last push 2025-04-01
ZimaOS Blue is IceWhale's MIT-licensed local-first agent runtime, 'inspired by OpenClaw'
ZimaDocs local LLM guide: llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible server on an NVIDIA GPU (CC >= 8.0, >= 16 GB VRAM); a coding agent may be granted 'socket level' (Docker socket) permission to set it up
ZimaOS remote access: ZimaClient encrypted peer-to-peer channel; open-protocol alternatives in the official store are Tailscale, WireGuard Easy, Firefly and NetBird
ZimaOS Backup app: from-to tasks (Cloud, LAN, USB, Zima sources) with versions and schedules; the 1.8.0 rootfs ships rsync and rclone but no restic, borg or kopia

ZimaOS SECURITY.md lists 11 published CVEs (2024-2026), including CVE-2026-21891 auth bypass (9.4) and CVE-2026-28798 internal service access via /v1/sys/proxy (9.1); only the latest version is in scope
Issue #557: an update looked successful in the UI but slot B kernel-panicked (slow second NVMe); RAUC fell back to A each time with no user-visible error
Issue #549: Docker 28.x mount churn knocked NetworkManager, logind, polkit and rauc off the system bus on every boot (1.6.1-1.7.0-beta2); mitigated by rolling Docker back to 27.5.1
Issue #478 '[Beta][Bug] Corrupt Services and boot' (2026-04-19) is open; only title and state read
CasaOS to ZimaOS has no in-place upgrade: the documented path is a fresh ZimaOS install, SMB file copy and the third-party CTOZ tool for apps
Release 1.5.0 auto-upgraded devices that updated promptly to ZimaOS Plus
The 1.8.0 release build's os-release CPE_NAME carries 'development' in its update field
ZimaOS has shipped NVIDIA drivers as systemd-sysext images on the data disk (nvidia-open-kernel-580.105.08-linux-6.12.25.raw in /DATA/.extensions), which the 1.8.0 hook removes
The 1.8.0 rootfs has 151 entries in /etc/apparmor.d (upstream profile set); whether AppArmor is enforced at runtime was not checked
